name: Josef "The Cavalier" Tadeuscz
caption: Won a 15-man tournament at The Grand European to become the first EEF European Heavyweight Champion.

name: "Normal" Klaus Lehman
caption: Won a twelve-man battle royal at Survival of the Fittest to claim the vacant EEF European Heavyweight Championship; ranked #159 on the RSPWF community's own 1997 Top 200 under this fed's tag.

identity.note: The same billing exists in other wings; this entity was minted from its own federation's 1997 documents with no receipt joining it to those — held distinct under the no-auto-merge-and-no-silent-distinctness rule; reopenable on a shared-handler or cross-fed receipt.

name: "Classic" Andrew Archer
caption: Founding-roster wrestler who won the Grand European's own Royal Rumble for a bye into its semi-finals, and holds the EEF German Championship, though a rival billed himself the 'Real GERMAN CHAMPION' that December in a dispute never resolved.

name: Marquis "The King" Sia

tenures.source: EEF's own served Grand European PPV text, part 6 of 8 (18 August 1997, msg_id uEA76ZrBU3cJ): ring-announced with James Bane, led by manager Queen Victoria, as "the tagteam know as the Monarchy," wrestling directly to beat the Wild Beasts in the tag tournament semifinal. Part 7 of 8 (msg_id E0bHaKOxXtcJ): the Monarchy beat the Italian Stallions to become the first EEF Tag Team Champions, Sia making the winning cover after Bane's Royal Sceptre shot.

caption: One half of The Monarchy, making the winning cover after James Bane's Royal Sceptre shot to help make the team the first EEF Tag Team Champions, beating the Italian Stallions in the Grand European final.

name: James "The Squire" Bane

tenures.source: EEF's own served Grand European PPV text, part 6 of 8 (18 August 1997, msg_id uEA76ZrBU3cJ): ring-announced with Marquis Sia, led by manager Queen Victoria, as "the tagteam know as the Monarchy," wrestling directly to beat the Wild Beasts in the tag tournament semifinal. Part 7 of 8 (msg_id E0bHaKOxXtcJ): the Monarchy beat the Italian Stallions to become the first EEF Tag Team Champions, Bane hitting Antonio with the Royal Sceptre just before Sia's winning cover.

caption: One half of The Monarchy, hitting Antonio with the Royal Sceptre to help make the team the first EEF Tag Team Champions, beating the Italian Stallions in the Grand European final.
